import MumfordLib.AffineSimplexChains
import MumfordLib.SingularAffineSimplexGeometry

/-!
# A barycentric cone producer for singular subdivision

The full barycentric subdivision operator is assembled inductively from cones on
faces.  This file records the chain-level producer used by that induction: for
an ordered affine simplex, cone from its barycenter.  Its boundary formula is
the required prism identity, so later subdivision code can use the operator
without unfolding the affine parametrization.
-/

set_option autoImplicit false

noncomputable section

open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite
open scoped Simplicial

namespace Mumford.Analytic

variable {m n : ℕ}

/-- The affine cone on an ordered `n`-simplex, using its barycenter as cone
vertex.  This is the degree-`n` producer used in the inductive subdivision
construction. -/
def affineBarycentricConeChain (m n : ℕ) :
    (VertexListChainComplex (stdSimplex ℝ (Fin (m + 1)))).X n ⟶
      (IntegralSingularChainComplex
        (TopCat.of (stdSimplex ℝ (Fin (m + 1))))).X (n + 1) :=
  Sigma.desc fun v ↦
    singularSimplexChain
      (affineSingularSimplex
        (Fin.cons (affineSimplexBarycenter v) v))

@[reassoc (attr := simp)]
theorem vertexListChain_affineBarycentricConeChain
    (v : Fin (n + 1) → stdSimplex ℝ (Fin (m + 1))) :
    vertexListChain v ≫ affineBarycentricConeChain m n =
      singularSimplexChain
        (affineSingularSimplex
          (Fin.cons (affineSimplexBarycenter v) v)) :=
  Sigma.ι_desc _ _

/-- The barycentric cone producer satisfies the prism boundary identity. -/
@[reassoc]
theorem vertexListChain_affineBarycentricConeChain_boundary
    (v : Fin (n + 2) → stdSimplex ℝ (Fin (m + 1))) :
    vertexListChain v ≫ affineBarycentricConeChain m (n + 1) ≫
        (IntegralSingularChainComplex
          (TopCat.of (stdSimplex ℝ (Fin (m + 1))))).d (n + 2) (n + 1) =
      singularSimplexChain (affineSingularSimplex v) -
        ∑ i : Fin (n + 2), (-1 : ℤ) ^ i.val •
          singularSimplexChain
            (affineSingularSimplex
              (Fin.cons (affineSimplexBarycenter v)
                (v ∘ i.succAbove))) := by
  rw [vertexListChain_affineBarycentricConeChain_assoc,
    affineSingularSimplex_cone_boundary]

/-! The recursive barycentric subdivision operator on ordered vertex lists. -/

/-- The degreewise barycentric subdivision endomorphism.

In positive degree, a simplex is first replaced by the signed sum of the
subdivisions of its faces, and then coned from its barycenter.  This is the
usual recursive definition of barycentric subdivision, expressed directly on
the free ordered-list chain complex.
-/
def barycentricSubdivision (m : ℕ) :
    (n : ℕ) →
      (VertexListChainComplex (stdSimplex ℝ (Fin (m + 1)))).X n ⟶
        (VertexListChainComplex (stdSimplex ℝ (Fin (m + 1)))).X n
  := Nat.rec (motive := fun n ↦
      (VertexListChainComplex (stdSimplex ℝ (Fin (m + 1)))).X n ⟶
        (VertexListChainComplex (stdSimplex ℝ (Fin (m + 1)))).X n)
      (𝟙 _) (fun n f ↦ Sigma.desc fun v ↦
        vertexListChain v ≫
          (VertexListChainComplex (stdSimplex ℝ (Fin (m + 1)))).d (n + 1) n ≫
          f ≫ vertexListCone (affineSimplexBarycenter v) n)

@[reassoc (attr := simp)]
theorem vertexListChain_barycentricSubdivision_succ
    (v : Fin (n + 2) → stdSimplex ℝ (Fin (m + 1))) :
    vertexListChain v ≫ barycentricSubdivision m (n + 1) =
      vertexListChain v ≫
        (VertexListChainComplex (stdSimplex ℝ (Fin (m + 1)))).d (n + 1) n ≫
        barycentricSubdivision m n ≫
        vertexListCone (affineSimplexBarycenter v) n :=
  Sigma.ι_desc _ _


end Mumford.Analytic
